host_reports.name: actor
host_reports.method:
Host differential test for viewport culls and unchanged actor geometry.

Compile the actual old/new C draw functions against one pure deterministic
depth stub and the original OAM writer. Exhaustive native viewport edges and
random canvases compare all OAM bytes and Actor bytes, including full OAM,
hurt blinking, hidden actors and blades visible while their owner is outside
the viewport. This establishes cull equivalence; actual forest depth and
gameplay are qualified separately in the mGBA comparison suite.

host_reports.name: effects
host_reports.method:
Compare the original and optimized glitter selection/HUD map algorithms.

The actual C source from the baseline revision and current checkout is compiled
for the host, with deterministic room/actor/render fixtures. Glitter calls,
ordering, priorities, frame counters and HUD shadow-map bytes must agree.
This establishes algorithm equivalence, not native GBA timing or full-game
visual correctness; the separate mGBA performance/render runs cover those.

host_reports.name: visibility
host_reports.method:
Compare packed canopy queries and Bloom guard against the original pixels.

Host execution maps a private fake GBA VRAM range, varies actual live entries,
tile alpha/flips, room bounds, legacy foliage and both tree planes, and compares
the optimized row query with32 original scalar calls. The complete original
prepare_canopy_visibility function is read from the frozen baseline revision;
all133 native poses, palette classifications, flips and both tree priorities
are compared byte-for-byte, including diagnostics and queue arguments. This
also compares240,000 depth queries with the complete original priority
function, varying planted owner rows and native body bounds. This is a
pure-query/guard equivalence check, not an emulator performance claim.

host_reports.name: objects
host_reports.method:
Compare actual object/hand painters after pool-kind rejection.

The original/candidate functions and their release-overlap helpers execute on
identical96-actor pools. The unchanged renderer/native sheet descriptors and
a deterministic pure terrain-priority stub record every painter call, OAM
byte and all gameplay state bytes. Fixtures include released loads, arrows,
flames, eight-frame bomb handoff, gated hoards, hidden/hurt states and full OAM.
Actual scene rendering/cycles remain the native performance suite's scope.

host_reports.name: system
host_reports.method:
Differential host qualification for animation scheduling and torch caching.

The actual baseline/candidate animation C functions run against all three
linked ROM descriptor/payload sets and synthetic valid byte-sized descriptors.
Recorded DMA destinations, ordered bytes, palette writes and volatile clock
read counts must match. Explicit clock-read fixtures model wrap, reset and
interrupt changes between the due test and frame selection. These host tests
do not replace real mGBA progression, framebuffer or cycle measurements.

torches.method:
Differential test of the unlit-torch cache through actual room write APIs.

The original/candidate room mutation and torch-count C functions are compiled
against native ROM metadata. Video/forest/interactive rendering is stubbed,
while room geometry, collision rebuilding and barrier-substrate selection use
the extracted C. Preview-details uses its actual save/restore function with a
disclosed deterministic generator stub that calls the real room write APIs.
No generator, game, art or ARM build is changed by this test.

host_reports.name: menu
host_reports.method:
Exact native map/kit output tests for the small cold-menu optimizations.

Compile the actual old/new BG-map prefixes and kit-cache C functions. Compare
all1024 map entries, every ordered write, all four native kit flips, opacity
masks and glyph bit masks for the three linked frame styles. Palette roles
are tested across all16 banks; cache warm/cold behavior is retained. The real
nine style/color menu-frame comparison is a separate mGBA test.
